steps.label: Q
steps.reason: The aromatic aldehyde has no α-hydrogen and undergoes intermolecular Cannizzaro disproportionation, giving both the corresponding benzyl alcohol and oxidized dicarboxylic acid after workup, while the carboxylic acid is first neutralized by NaOH.

steps.label: T
steps.reason: TsCl/pyridine conventionally tosylates the benzylic alcohol, but the unprotected carboxylic acid can also form a carboxylate and consume or react with TsCl, so without further conditions a unique major product cannot be assigned.

steps.label: U
steps.reason: Hot aqueous NaOH opens the epoxide by attack at its less substituted carbon to give a diol, then Kolbe–Schmitt carboxylation occurs at the phenol’s only free ortho position.

steps.label: S
steps.reason: The substrate has two nonequivalent secondary alcohols, and TsCl/pyridine can tosylate either or both; without specified stoichiometry or conditions, no unique major product can be assigned.

steps.label: T
steps.reason: Iodide preferentially displaces the tosylate at the secondary benzylic carbon, while the less reactive tosylate and aryl–alkyl ether remain intact under the standard one-equivalent outcome.

steps.label: U
steps.reason: HI can substitute the benzylic secondary OH, the other secondary OH, or cleave the aryl–alkyl ether at its alkyl side, and one equivalent alone does not specify a unique chemoselective outcome.

events.route: 1. Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of P: Aryl group migrates preferentially over methyl, giving Q = 4-(3-hydroxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)phenyl acetate. 2. Q to R: CH2N2/HBF4 methylates the alcohol to a methyl ether, R = 4-(3-methoxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)phenyl acetate. 3. R to S: Hydrolysis of the aryl acetate gives 4-(3-methoxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)phenol and acetic acid. Since S is one of the products, we need to check the options. Wait, S is a product of hydrolysis. Since R is an acetate ester, hydrolysis yields acetic acid and a phenol. 4. Q to T: TsCl tosylates the primary alcohol. 5. R to U: Lindlar reduction of alkyne to cis-alkene. 6. U to V: Bromination of alkene gives a vicinal dibromide.
events.student_must_notice: In Baeyer-Villiger, the aryl group has a higher migratory aptitude than the methyl group, leading to an aryl acetate, not a methyl ester.
events.trap: If the methyl group migrates, Q would be methyl 4-(3-hydroxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)benzoate, leading to S being 4-(3-methoxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)benzoic acid instead of acetic acid.

Consider the following reaction scheme starting with P (1-[4-(3-hydroxyprop-1-yn-1-yl)phenyl]ethan-1-one):

P --[mCPBA]--> Q
Q --[CH₂N₂, HBF₄]--> R
R --[(i) aq. NaOH, heat; (ii) H₃O⁺]--> S (where S is the lower molecular weight organic product)
Q --[TsCl, pyridine]--> T
R --[H₂, Pd/BaSO₄, quinoline]--> U
U --[Br₂, CCl₄]--> V

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.A: S has a degree of unsaturation of 1 and contains 1 sp2 hybridized carbon atom.
options.B: S is an aromatic compound that decolourises bromine water.
options.C: Compound U exhibits geometrical isomerism and contains 6 pi bonds.
options.D: Compound V contains exactly 2 stereocentres and exists as 4 stereoisomers.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P (p-acetyl phenyl propargyl alcohol) undergoes Baeyer–Villiger oxidation with mCPBA: the aryl group migrates preferentially over methyl, giving Q = 4-(3-hydroxyprop-1-ynyl)phenyl acetate (Ar–O–COCH3, with –C≡C–CH2OH para). CH2N2/HBF4 methylates the free alcohol, so R = Ar–O–COCH3 with –C≡C–CH2OCH3 (an aryl acetate bearing an internal-izable propargyl ether; the alkyne and the acetate are the key functional groups). (i) aq. NaOH, heat hydrolyzes the acetate ester, and (ii) H3O+ gives S = acetic acid, CH3COOH, molecular formula C2H4O2 → (A) is TRUE. Acetic acid has only 1 sp2 carbon (the carboxyl carbon), not 7 → (B) is FALSE (statement B would fit an aromatic acid, contradicting formula C2H4O2, so the aromatic ring is not part of S). R, containing the –C≡C– fragment, on Lindlar reduction (H2, Pd/BaSO4, quinoline) gives U, the cis (Z)-alkene Ar–CH=CH–CH2OCH3 fragment; a cis-alkene with different substituents on each carbon exhibits geometrical isomerism → (C) is TRUE. Br2/CCl4 adds anti across the double bond of U to give the vicinal dibromide V; both alkene carbons become stereocentres (each bears H, Br, and two different carbon groups), so V contains 2 stereocentres → (D) is TRUE. Correct options: A, C, D.
